non_blocking_notes: Audit callback contract is trust boundary — caller must not grant identity/provider authority via the callback mechanism; documentation explicit on this (WORK_QUEUE.md fixture security note)
Size limit (32KB) is implementation choice; if observations exceed this, caller-supplied normalization fails closed as designed
result.reasoning_summary: FW-SAAS-002 implements strict caller-supplied SaaS observation normalization with deterministic entry-point validation and Evidence-first, fail-closed semantics. All acceptance criteria met: (1) Providers, observation types, and indicators enforced via 4-element, 4-element, and 7-element allowlists with exact match validation; (2) References, fixture size, indicators count, and time/tenant bounds strictly bounded with SaaSObservationDenied on any violation; (3) SaaSObservation is frozen dataclass with trust=UNTRUSTED_DATA and mode/action defaults (DRY_RUN/DETECT_ONLY); (4) Indicators deterministically sorted before return; (5) Evidence logged before return with deployment=DISABLED; (6) Evidence dict excludes application_ref, principal_ref, target_ref (verified by both design and test assertion); (7) No provider API, OAuth exchange, token/credential access, network, SaaS mutation, containment, remediation, deployment, or response authority added. Test suite covers positive path (immutability, ordering, Evidence presence/minimization, untrusted defaults), 11 fail-closed boundary cases (tenant, provider, type, indicators, fields, references, time), and Evidence-callback failure mode. Patch is narrow, deterministic, and exhibits fail-closed behavior on all input validation failures.
